title: Demote a release
summary: The confirmation for demoting Diceroll 1.8.0 from stable on Oct 7, over the Release tracks page as it was before: what the demote does to the track, an optional reason, and what changes on each channel after a readiness check, with an outcome on every row and Steam skipped because it isn't connected.
compare: Opens from a lane's ⋯ menu or the release's page, over Release tracks as it was at 11:25 on Oct 7 (1.8.0 on stable since Oct 6, 1.8.1 already on beta). The accent is Release cyan.

The title is a question naming the release and the track; the first sentence says it leaves the stable track and stays on beta and dev, that stable goes back to 1.7.3, and that it can be promoted again. It never says delete, yank or remove.
Reason is labelled 'Optional · shown in Activity and on the release', uses the kit's standard field (not a focused look), and its text appears in the lane log afterwards.

Readiness runs before confirming. 'What changes' lists Diceroll's channels with an outcome at the right of every row, each fact once: Polaris Key '↓ Back to 1.7.3' (update checks and the download page; devices already on 1.8.0 keep it until a newer stable release), Google Play 'Halts at 20%' (Play can't go back a version) with the halt checkbox on, itch.io '↓ Back to 1.7.3' (windows-x64 and linux-x86_64), App Store 'Stays live' in warning with the fix-forward advice, Steam 'Skipped' (not connected, so 1.8.0 never reached it; Connect Steam). A skipped or blocked channel never blocks the others.
The foot is an outline Cancel and the primary 'Demote 1.8.0 from stable' with a down arrow; not a danger button, because promoting again undoes it.
After confirming, the page becomes packages.release-tracks: stable on 1.7.3, the demote in both logs, and, when a channel fails, the partial-success toast and lane callout with Retry.
Phone: the kit's bottom sheet; each channel row's outcome drops under its text, and the buttons are pinned full width with the primary on top, as on every dialog in the area.

Brand v2 shell (lead B2–B5, 2026-10-09): the work sits on the inset canvas with a 3px rule in the page's context accent (full-bleed below 1024); one orientation line (context chip + crumbs, never 'Platform' on a product page, no eyebrow repeating the path); h1 36/44 on a collection, 32/40 on a record, 24/32 on a phone; the one filled primary is ink and selection is ink, the accent marks context only; the selected nav item is the subtle fill with a 3px marker; card heads are bands with no numerals; route tabs are an underline tablist with a 3px indicator; tables with filters are one workbench band; weights 400/500/600.

Masthead mark (B4): from 1024px a 48px flat tile on this page (the feature's glyph on a landing page, the product's icon on a product page) replaces the orientation chip; below 1024 the chip carries the context; never on a dense data page, a record or a state page.
Ship builds is one identity (B5): Release cyan rule, chip, tile and nav marker, the Package glyph, crumb '<Product> › Ship builds'; no per-page green or tangerine.

Dialog and drawer head (B4): a 3px rule in the origin's accent along the top (none on a destructive or cautious confirmation), a head band with a hairline, one leading glyph or none (severity on a confirmation, the subject's mark on a record, never a service tile), title at or under 20/28; blurred backdrop with a flat fallback under reduced transparency.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fixed: readiness runs first, every row has an outcome, Steam matches Home, and the partial failure is designed on the page it lands on.

findings.issue: [Missing state] Demote changes five channels at once, with no design for one of them failing: no pre-check row and only a total-success toast.
findings.resolution: Readiness runs before confirming: Steam is a 'Skipped' row (1.8.0 never reached Steam because it isn't connected; Connect Steam) and the demote stays allowed for the other channels. The after-state on packages.release-tracks is a partial success: a warning toast 'Demoted 1.8.0, except on itch.io' with Retry, and a stable-lane callout 'itch.io still serves 1.8.0' with 'Retry itch.io'; the Home attention item is noted in compare for the products area.

findings.issue: [Copy/form] Reason doesn't say Optional; only the App Store row has an outcome; 'keep it until 1.8.1' names a version that didn't exist; the textarea reads as selected; the phone foot is side by side.
findings.resolution: Label: 'Reason · Optional · shown in Activity and on the release'. Every row has an outcome: 'Back to 1.7.3' (accent) for Polaris Key and itch.io, 'Halts at 20%' for Google Play, 'Stays live' (warning) for the App Store, 'Skipped' for Steam. Polaris Key reads '…keep it until a newer release reaches stable'. The textarea drops its focus state and uses the kit's standard field fill (--pk-surface-sunken; the kit's fields aren't white). The phone foot is the kit's sheet, primary full width.

findings.issue: [Cross-area consistency] products.home says Diceroll's Steam channel can't upload builds (no Steamworks publisher key), yet Release tracks, Demote and Updates (Godot) show Steam working normally; Home also omits the App Store and itch.io.
findings.resolution: Kept Home's story (and distribution.channels', where Steam is 'Not set up, step 2 of 4'). Every Steam cell on Release tracks says 'Not sent: Steam isn't connected', with an attention row and Connect Steam under the map; Demote and Promote list Steam as 'Skipped' with Connect Steam; Updates (Godot) marks Steam 'Not connected'. Also aligned with distribution.channels: itch.io's channels are windows-x64 and linux-x86_64 and Diceroll has no macOS build, so the Godot updater covers Windows and Linux. Home omitting the App Store and itch.io belongs to the products area.

findings.issue: [Copy: sentence case] Sentences start with lower-case track names ('beta, dev and your own tracks…', 'stable is back on 1.7.3', 'stable goes back to 1.7.3'); 'beta · also gets stable' is ambiguous.
findings.resolution: No sentence starts with a lower-case track name any more: 'Every license gets the stable track. Beta, dev and your own tracks…', 'Stable is back on 1.7.3…', 'Stable, beta and dev use the default lanes', 'Stable goes back to 1.7.3'. Lane lines read 'Built in · beta licenses also get stable' and 'Built in · dev licenses also get beta'. Track tags stay lower-case mono because they are identifiers.

findings.issue: The phone sheet clips rows and the descriptions repeat the lane page.
findings.resolution: Descriptions cut to one clause; sheet is .dialog.scroll.fade at 90vh (the last rows scroll under a fade, the foot stays pinned); Cancel is a text button on phone; the CTA uses the warning token (.btn.warn-fill); reason caption 'Optional, shown in Activity'; the Google Play outcome carries data-unchecked="Stays at 20%" for the real build (a static mockup cannot toggle).
